nodes.title: Desktop entry (main)
nodes.description: Binary entry point. Builds the 1400x900 Workbench window, injects style.css into the page head and launches the Dioxus desktop runtime with the App root component.

nodes.title: App root & header
nodes.description: Root component. Resolves the working directory from argv[1] or the current dir, optionally opens a file from argv[2], provides AppState as context and starts the Workbench session coroutine. It reloads .workbench data when cwd or repo_version changes. The header has the graph toggle, folder picker (rfd), the provider and model picker, model and cost badges, a warning badge in Full auto mode, a branch picker and a New session button. The branch picker shows the current branch and opens a filterable list of local and remote branches; picking one runs git switch (remote-only branches get a local tracking branch), and typing a new name offers to create it. open_folder switches the working folder (used by the folder picker and the project view), and a project chip in the header jumps to the project that contains the open folder. The header also shows the self-updater's button when a newer build is available on GitHub.

nodes.title: AppState (signals store)
nodes.description: Central reactive store made of Dioxus signals: graph, baseline, rules, related GitHub repos, the MCP connections and their last reported status, the user's provider settings, the projects list and whether the project view is showing, selection, the module scope path (which network the graph view shows), chat items, session id, model, cost, the chat mode and a plan waiting for approval, open file, tabs and the active job. It also holds the domain actions: open/save/revert files, load and sync the workbench from disk, update and save the graph or the current network, enter and leave modules, compute changes against the baseline, revert node and module changes, mark the graph as in sync, and update rules, related repos and MCP connections (saving MCP connections restarts Workbench on the next message). For plain chat turns it snapshots the graph when the turn starts and, when the turn succeeds, moves the graph edits Workbench made into the baseline (the whole graph if it was in sync, otherwise only Workbench's changes), so they don't show up as the user's pending changes. Edits the user makes in the graph during the turn stay pending. Also defines the Cmd enum sent to the session loop.

nodes.title: Workbench session loop
nodes.description: Long-running coroutine that receives Cmd values (Send, Prompt, Interrupt, Restart) and owns the live agent. With Workbench it spawns the agent process lazily, respawns it when the rules version changes, and resumes the stored session id. A generation counter drops events from killed processes. Streamed events become chat items; file-touching tool results bump repo_version and reload the open file, and Done finishes the current graph job. Every delivered message outside a job starts a chat turn in app-state, which Done settles against the baseline. Changing a project's repositories or descriptions also restarts Workbench with the updated project context. When it spawns the agent it passes the enabled MCP connections as --mcp-config, and the MCP statuses from the agent's init event go to app-state. With any other provider every message starts a new turn through the agent layer, and only Workbench sessions are remembered for the session history.

nodes.title: Workbench agent process
nodes.description: Finds the agent binary, then spawns it with stream-json input/output, partial messages, the permission mode of the chat mode, AskUserQuestion turned off (the agent asks in its reply instead), an optional --resume, --model, --append-system-prompt and --mcp-config. It writes user messages, interrupt control requests and permission answers (a plan approval also sets the session's mode) to stdin. Stdout lines are parsed into AgentEvent values (Init with the MCP server statuses, TextDelta, ToolUse, ToolResult, Done, Stderr, Exited) and tagged with a generation number. Also provides tool summaries and file-path extraction.

nodes.title: Workbench agent CLI
nodes.description: The external agent executable, run as a subprocess in the project directory. It does the actual agent work (reading and editing files, writing .workbench/graph.json) and streams JSON events back.

nodes.title: Prompt builder
nodes.description: Builds every structured prompt sent to Workbench: generate or refresh the architecture graph (with the JSON schema, including modules), draft nodes into the network the user is looking at, process graph changes into code edits (new, removed and edited modules and attachments included; Workbench may add nodes for new units it had to create), debug a flow (several modes), audit code against rules, ask about a node, review a pull request, and the per-session system-prompt append, which tells Workbench to keep the graph in step with every code change (files, new nodes for new units, removed nodes, updated descriptions and links), plus, when the open folder belongs to a project, the project's name and the other repositories (folder, GitHub name, description) Workbench may read, the modules guide, enabled rules and the related GitHub repositories.

nodes.title: Graph model
nodes.description: Serde types Node, Flow, Module and Graph, plus helpers: lookup, unique ids, slugify, node removal, edges, auto-layout into columns, kind colours, and diff(base, current), which produces field-level Change records. A Module is an isolated node network stored in graph.modules; a node whose `module` field names it is an attachment point, and one module can be attached in many places (never inside itself). The diff covers the main network, every module network and module title/description, tagging each change with its scope. absorb applies a set of changes from a current graph onto a baseline. load and save read and write the graph JSON under .workbench.

nodes.title: Rules model
nodes.description: Project rules (id, title, body, enabled, optional node scope) stored in .workbench/rules.json. Provides load and save, id generation, filtering of rules relevant to a set of nodes, and rendering rules as prompt text.

nodes.title: .workbench data files
nodes.description: On-disk JSON store in the opened project: graph.json (the current, editable graph), graph.baseline.json (the last state in sync with the code) and rules.json. These files are read on load and re-read whenever the repo version changes.

nodes.title: Project working tree
nodes.description: The opened folder's source files and git repository. The editor and Workbench both read and write files here, and git commands run against it.

nodes.title: Graph tab & toolbar
nodes.description: Hosts the canvas with the floating chat and, on its right, the node menu with the Node, Flows, Changes, History and Prompt panes. The toolbar adds nodes and starts a Generate job, which sends the mapping prompt to Workbench with the graph locked until the job finishes. The nodes have draggable inputs and outputs so they're easily able to change their links. The breadcrumb row always shows project › repository › modules, and Up from the repository root opens the project view. The node menu can be hidden and resized by dragging the splitter to its left; its width and open state are saved in the workbench layout.

nodes.title: Prompt pane (add nodes from prompt)
nodes.description: Graph sub-tab where the user describes behaviour in plain text. Add nodes starts a Draft job that asks Workbench to extend graph.json with new nodes, links and flows without touching source code. Because a Draft job never updates the baseline, the new nodes show up as pending changes that are committed into code afterwards.

nodes.title: Chat modes (Plan / Accept edits / Auto / Full auto)
nodes.description: One mode decides both how the agent acts and what it may do without asking; the toggle sits under the chat and every session starts in Plan. Plan is read only: Workbench runs in its own plan mode and presents its plan with ExitPlanMode, which Workbench turns into a prompt asking whether to run it in Auto, Full auto or Accept edits, or keep planning; picking a mode answers the request and switches the running session's mode. Other providers get plan instructions instead, and their plan-mode reply gets the same prompt, which then asks them to implement the plan. Accept edits asks before every change and command, Auto answers every permission request itself except deleting files, and Full auto never asks. For Draft and Process jobs, Plan mode also lets Workbench ask numbered questions ending in a marker, pausing the job until the user answers.

nodes.title: Graph canvas
nodes.description: SVG and HTML node diagram with pan, zoom, fit-to-view, node dragging (saves the position) and link creation by clicking. It highlights the active flow path and colours nodes by kind. It always shows one network: the main graph or the module the user has opened. Module attachment nodes are drawn with a double teal border, the module name and node count, and are marked edited when their module has pending changes; double-clicking one opens the module, and a breadcrumb bar leads back up. The toolbar's + Module… menu creates a new module or attaches an existing one here. A press in the canvas or on a node fades the floating chat.

nodes.title: Node inspector
nodes.description: Editor for the selected node's title, kind, description, files and links. It shows incoming callers, can revert the node to the baseline, and has an Ask Workbench action that sends a node-specific question. Here a node holds a explicit list of links to other nodes. One list of inputs flows and one for output flows. The nodes also hold a list of the files that is related to it and in what manner, like its own dependencies, where its used and such. For reference nodes it shows the source, its detected type, whether it is a Workbench project, and a picker for the referenced project's nodes.

nodes.title: Changes pane (commit graph)
nodes.description: Lists the field-level differences between the current graph and the baseline, including nodes inside modules (labelled with their module) and added, removed or edited modules. Show opens the right module and selects the node. With an optional note, it sends a Process job that asks Workbench to change the code to match the edited graph. When the job succeeds, the baseline is updated.

nodes.title: Flows pane & debug
nodes.description: Lists flows, lets the user draft new ones by clicking nodes in order, and highlights the active flow on the canvas. Runs a debug prompt for a flow in the chosen DebugMode, with an optional symptom description.

nodes.title: Rules view
nodes.description: CRUD list of project rules: add, edit, enable or disable, scope to a node, delete, and filter. An Audit action asks Workbench to check the codebase against all enabled rules. Any change bumps rules_version, which restarts the Workbench process on the next message.

nodes.title: Chat pane
nodes.description: Conversation view showing user messages, labelled prompts, streaming assistant markdown, tool calls with results, info lines and errors. The input box sends Cmd::Send and has a Stop button for Cmd::Interrupt while busy.

nodes.title: Code pane (Files / Editor / Diff)
nodes.description: Right-hand tabs. Files lists tracked and untracked files with their git status. Diff shows a syntax-highlighted git diff against a chosen base, and each hunk has an Ask Workbench button that pastes it into the chat input. Editor hosts the CodeMirror view. The GitHub tab hosts the GitHub module, the MCP tab hosts the MCP module, and the Providers tab hosts the LLM providers module.

nodes.title: CodeMirror editor bridge
nodes.description: Mounts the bundled CodeMirror 6 editor (vim mode, many languages) in the webview through document.eval. Load and focus messages go to JS; Change, Save (:w), Close (:q) and Reload (:e) messages come back and update the open file in AppState.

nodes.title: Git service
nodes.description: Thin wrapper over the git CLI: repo detection, current branch, branch listing, switching and creating branches, porcelain status, ls-files, pushing the current branch, and a diff against a base that includes untracked files. It parses the output into FileDiff, Hunk and DiffLine values, and each hunk can be turned back into a patch. For the node history it reads git log -p of the history file and maps each entry's uid to the commit, reachable from HEAD, that first added its line.

nodes.title: Build & install tooling
nodes.description: Makefile targets for run, test, install, open, uninstall and the editor bundle build. install.sh builds a release binary, packages it as ~/Applications/Workbench.app and installs a `wbrs` launcher in ~/.local/bin. `make editor` uses esbuild to bundle editor-js into src/editor.bundle.js. Before building it checks for git, curl, cargo and, on Linux, make, a C compiler, pkg-config and the GUI libraries. It lists what's missing with the exact install commands (pacman, apt, dnf, zypper, apk or xbps; rustup for Rust; Xcode Command Line Tools on macOS) and runs them only after the user confirms on the terminal. It stops with an explanation on Debian/Ubuntu releases too old to have WebKitGTK 4.1. If the folder isn't a git checkout (a ZIP download), it offers to link it to the GitHub repo so the update check works, stashing any files that differ from main.

nodes.title: Workbench layout
nodes.description: The window body under the header: the projects sidebar on the left and the workbench on the right. The workbench switches between the Graph, Code and Rules views, shows workbench load errors, and shows the project view when a project is picked. The layout (sidebar open, node menu width and open state, chat anchor, expanded and locked) is saved in ~/.config/workbench/layout.json.

nodes.title: GitHub (PRs & repos)
nodes.description: The Code pane's GitHub tab. Here the module is used interactively: list, read, review, comment on, open and merge pull requests, and browse related repositories.

nodes.title: GitHub (related repos context)
nodes.description: The prompt builder uses the module's related-repository list so every Workbench session knows which other GitHub projects it may read with gh for context.

nodes.title: External references
nodes.description: Nodes of kind `reference` point outside the project through `reference.source`: a local folder or file, a GitHub repository (URL, owner/repo or github:owner/repo@ref/path), a website, or an npm/crate/pypi/go package. Sources are parsed into a Source, and Workbench looks for the referenced project's .workbench/graph.json: locally by walking up from the path, on GitHub through gh at the path and its parents, or in node_modules and the cargo registry for packages. Loaded graphs are cached in AppState by source. The user can pick nodes of that graph into `reference.nodes`, and their descriptions and files are put into the system prompt, the selection context and process prompts as read-only context.

nodes.title: Module inspector
nodes.description: Shown in the Node sub-tab when a module is open and no node is selected. Edits the module's title and description, lists every place the module is attached (click to jump there), shows pending module changes with Revert, and deletes the module together with its attachment nodes.

nodes.title: Ghost branches
nodes.description: Shows the graph work on other git branches as read-only ghost nodes on the canvas. For each branch the user picks from the Ghosts toggle, it reads the branch's .workbench/graph.json and the one at the merge base with HEAD, and diffs them so only that branch's own work appears: added nodes become dashed ghosts with dashed links, and nodes it changed or removed get a coloured ring. Clicking a ghost puts it into Workbench's context next to the selected nodes, with a note to read its code via git show instead of checking the branch out.

nodes.title: Project view (related repositories)
nodes.description: The level above a repository's graph. A project, such as Workbench, groups the local clones of the repositories that make up one product, for example frontend, backend and host. It shows each repository as a node with an editable description text box beside it instead of links, plus its graph size and GitHub remote. Projects are stored in ~/.config/workbench/projects.json and listed in the projects sidebar; the inspector sits on the right and the floating chat sits over the canvas; double-clicking a repository opens it as the working folder and shows its graph. When the open folder belongs to a project, the other repositories and their descriptions go into Workbench's system prompt.

nodes.title: Node history
nodes.description: Shared, append-only history of node and module changes (title, kind, module, reference, links, files and description) stored as before/after text. Each entry has a unique id, a time, an author (git user.name) and a source: a person in Workbench, Workbench working for that person, or an edit outside Workbench. The log is .workbench/node-history.jsonl, one entry per line, with a .workbench/.gitattributes union-merge rule so logs from several people merge without conflicts; on load lines are de-duplicated by id and sorted by time. What this client last saw of the graph is kept locally in ~/.config/workbench/node-snapshots/, and a change already in the shared log (for example pulled from a teammate) is not logged again. Rapid edits by the same person are merged into one entry, and a built-in LCS line diff renders entries as classic +/− diffs.

nodes.title: History pane
nodes.description: Bottom-panel tab that lists recorded node and module changes newest first as classic line diffs, with who made each change (you, a teammate, Workbench, or outside Workbench) and when. When one node is selected (or a module is open) it can filter to just that node's history, and Show jumps to the node. The node inspector links here with a History (n) button. There is no clear action because the log is shared with the repo. In a git repository the list is grouped against the git state: an Uncommitted section first, for entries not yet in a commit on this branch, then one section per commit (short hash, subject, author, time), newest first. Each entry also carries an uncommitted or commit-hash tag.

nodes.title: Self-updater
nodes.description: Checks on startup whether GitHub's main branch has commits that the running build lacks. It compares the commit embedded at build time (build.rs) with main through the GitHub compare API using curl. If main is ahead, a header button opens and lists the new commits. Choosing Update fetches main into a private checkout under ~/.cache/workbench/source and builds it in the background. Restart now runs that checkout's install script in a detached process and reopens the current folder. If git or cargo is missing, it points the user to install.sh instead of starting the build.

nodes.title: MCP connections
nodes.description: The Code pane's MCP tab and the MCP config passed to the agent CLI in use. The user manages MCP server connections in the tab, and every enabled one goes to Workbench Code (--mcp-config), Codex (-c mcp_servers) or Vibe (VIBE_MCP_SERVERS) so the agent can call their tools. Workbench's reported connection status is shown back in the tab.

nodes.title: Agent layer
nodes.description: One interface over every LLM provider for the session loop. Workbench runs as the long-lived agent process; every other provider runs one turn per message, either a fresh Codex or Vibe process that resumes the previous session or one API request with the conversation so far. All of them report back as the same chat events. Only Workbench can be interrupted mid-turn or ask for permissions; other turns are stopped by killing them.

nodes.title: LLM providers
nodes.description: Lets the user switch the chat between Workbench Code, Codex and Mistral Vibe (agent CLIs) and the Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral and OpenRouter APIs, with a model per provider. The header uses it for the provider and model picker, the Code pane for the Providers tab, and the agent layer to run Codex, Vibe and API turns.

nodes.title: Projects sidebar
nodes.description: Collapsible list on the left of every project with its repositories and worktrees, read from the projects saved in ~/.config/workbench/projects.json. Under each project it lists every agent running in it, with its provider's logo, the folder it runs in and whether it is working or waiting for a prompt. Clicking a project shows its project view; clicking a repository, worktree or agent opens that folder. It can create a project and add a repository to a project.

nodes.title: Floating chat dock
nodes.description: The chat floats over the graph, code or rules view and can be anchored to the top, bottom, left or right. Top and bottom chats are centred and get their height from the focus: a press in the graph fades the chat to a peek at the latest reply, hovering shows it again and clicking it shows more of the conversation. The Expand toggle makes it larger and the Lock toggle stops graph clicks from fading it; left and right chats fill the height.

nodes.title: Agent activity
nodes.description: Finds the coding agents (Workbench Code, Codex, Vibe) running on this machine by reading /proc, which folder each runs in, and whether it is working (using CPU) or waiting for a prompt. Workbench's own session is added with the provider it uses, and every agent is given to the project repository or worktree it runs in. Each agent kind maps to its LLM company's logo (Workbench, OpenAI, Mistral, OpenRouter), drawn from Simple Icons path data.

nodes.title: Theme & dropdowns
nodes.description: theme.css holds every colour, radius, font and shadow as a CSS variable, plus the base control styles; style.css only uses these variables. The webview draws native <select> and <datalist> popups with the system theme, so dropdown.rs draws themed ones instead: Dropdown picks one of a list of choices, and ComboBox is a text field with suggestions, used for model names and node kinds. Their open list is fixed to the window and opens upwards when there is more room above.

flows.name: Send a chat message to Workbench
Open, edit and save a file
Review diff and ask Workbench about a hunk

modules.title: GitHub integration
modules.description: Talks to GitHub through the gh CLI so the user can read, write, review and merge pull requests of this project and read related repositories for context. Its interface is the GitHub tab component plus the related-repos list in AppState, which the prompt builder turns into Workbench context.

nodes.title: GitHub tab
nodes.description: Container with a repository selector (this repo or any related repo), sub-tabs for Pull requests, New PR and Related repos, and a reload button. Shares the selected repo, open PR and a reload counter with its children through a context.

nodes.title: Pull request list
nodes.description: Lists up to 50 pull requests of the selected repository filtered by open, closed, merged or all, with state, number, title, author, branches and review decision. Clicking one opens its detail view.

nodes.title: PR detail, review & merge
nodes.description: Shows a pull request's description, checks, reviews and comments, and its diff on demand. Posts comments, approvals and change requests, and merges with squash, merge or rebase (optionally deleting the branch) behind a confirm step. Ask Workbench to review sends a read-only review prompt to the chat.

nodes.title: New pull request
nodes.description: Opens a pull request from the current branch into the base branch (the default branch unless changed), with title, markdown body and draft flag, optionally pushing the branch first. Refuses to open one from the base branch. Draft with Workbench asks Workbench to write the title and description from the branch's commits.

nodes.title: Related repositories
nodes.description: Adds and removes related repositories (owner/repo or a github.com URL), jumps to a related repo's pull requests, and browses its files through the contents API. A file can be added to the chat input as context, truncated to keep prompts small.

nodes.title: GitHub service (gh CLI)
nodes.description: Wraps the gh CLI with prompts disabled: current and named repo info, list, view and diff pull requests (diffs parsed by the git service's parser), create, comment, review and merge, and read repository contents and raw files. Repository names and content paths are validated before they reach gh.

nodes.title: Related repos file
nodes.description: .workbench/github.json holds the list of related repositories. It is loaded with the rest of the workbench data, and saving it bumps the system-prompt version so Workbench restarts with the new context.

nodes.title: GitHub CLI (gh)
nodes.description: The external gh executable, authenticated with gh auth login. It runs in the project directory and talks to the GitHub API.

flows.name: Review and merge a pull request
Read a related repository for context

modules.title: MCP connections
modules.description: Lets Workbench call tools on MCP servers. The user configures servers (local stdio programs or remote http/sse URLs) in the MCP tab, they are saved to .workbench/mcp.json, and every enabled server is passed to the agent CLI in use (Workbench Code, Codex or Vibe). Its interface is the MCP tab plus the mcp_servers list in AppState.

nodes.title: MCP tab
nodes.description: Lists the project's MCP servers as cards. Each card has an enabled toggle, a name, a transport (stdio, http or sse), and either a command with arguments and environment lines or a URL with header lines. It shows the status Workbench reported for the server, or why it is not passed to Workbench yet.

nodes.title: MCP server model
nodes.description: The Server type and its transport, loading and saving of the MCP file, and claude_config, which turns the usable servers (enabled, named, with a command or URL) into the mcpServers JSON for --mcp-config. KEY=value and Name: value lines become env and header objects, which the Codex and Vibe runners reuse for their own config formats.

nodes.title: MCP connections file
nodes.description: .workbench/mcp.json holds the list of MCP servers. It is loaded with the rest of the workbench data and is committed with the project, so secrets should be written as ${ENV_VAR} references that Workbench expands.

nodes.title: MCP servers
nodes.description: The external MCP servers. The agent CLI in use starts the stdio ones as subprocesses and connects to the http/sse ones, then exposes their tools to the agent.

modules.title: LLM providers
modules.description: Switches the chat between agent CLIs installed on this machine (Workbench, Codex, Mistral Vibe) and direct chat APIs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral, OpenRouter). The chosen provider, a model per provider, API keys and loaded model lists are stored per user. Its interface is the header picker, the Providers tab and the Codex, Vibe and API runners the agent layer starts.

nodes.title: Provider & model picker
nodes.description: Settings controls for the provider and the model. Switching provider starts a new session, since sessions can't move between providers. Changing the model restarts the agent on the next message. The provider is a themed Dropdown and the model a ComboBox with the provider's model list as suggestions.

nodes.title: Providers tab
nodes.description: One card per provider, showing whether its CLI is installed or its API key is set, with a Use button. API providers get a key field and a Load models button that fetches the provider's live model list.

nodes.title: Provider catalogue & settings
nodes.description: The Provider enum: label, how it is reached (CLI binary or API base URL, key variable and API style), suggested models and availability. Settings holds the chosen provider, the model per provider, typed API keys (the environment variable wins) and loaded model lists.

nodes.title: Provider settings file
nodes.description: providers.json in the user's Workbench config folder, outside every project, so API keys are never committed.

nodes.title: Codex runner
nodes.description: Builds one `codex exec --json` turn (resume, model, sandbox from the chat mode, Workbench instructions as developer_instructions, MCP servers as -c overrides) and parses its JSONL events into chat events: thread id, messages, commands, file changes, MCP and web-search calls, and turn end or failure.

nodes.title: Vibe runner
nodes.description: Builds one `vibe -p --output streaming` turn (resume, agent from the chat mode, model and MCP servers through VIBE_* variables, Workbench instructions at the top of a new session's first prompt) and parses its history entries into chat events, skipping the entries a resumed session replays.

nodes.title: API chat client
nodes.description: Sends the conversation to the Anthropic Messages API or an OpenAI-style chat completions API (OpenAI, Mistral, OpenRouter) in one request and returns the answer. Also lists a provider's models. API providers only chat: no file edits, tools or MCP.

nodes.title: Codex CLI
nodes.description: The external `codex` executable from OpenAI, run once per message in the project folder.

nodes.title: Mistral Vibe CLI
nodes.description: The external `vibe` executable from Mistral, run once per message in the project folder.

nodes.title: Provider APIs
nodes.description: The HTTP APIs of Anthropic, OpenAI, Mistral and OpenRouter, called with the user's API keys.
